title: Full Mock Exam – All Chapters
description: 25-question comprehensive exam covering all 12 chapters of the FIDE Arbiter's Manual

questions.text: How early before a round should an arbiter arrive at the playing hall for the FIRST round of a tournament?

options.text: 15 minutes
30 minutes
1 hour
2 hours

questions.explanation: Per Article 1.2, for the first round of the tournament the arbiter should arrive at least one (1) hour before the start. For subsequent rounds, 30 minutes is the minimum.

questions.text: Which of the following is an acceptable behaviour for an arbiter while supervising games in progress?

options.text: Leaving the playing area every 15 minutes to smoke
Sitting at a computer surfing the internet
Actively observing all games, especially those in time trouble
Speaking on their mobile phone in the playing hall

questions.explanation: Per Article 1.1, arbiters must observe all games especially in time trouble. Leaving the area frequently, surfing the internet, or using mobile phones are all explicitly prohibited behaviours.

questions.text: What is the objective of each player in a game of chess?

options.text: To capture all of the opponent's pieces
To place the opponent's king under attack with no legal escape (checkmate)
To occupy the four central squares
To promote a pawn first

questions.explanation: Per FIDE Laws Article 1.1, the objective of each player is to place the opponent's king 'under attack in such a way that the opponent has no legal move.' This is called checkmate.

questions.text: Under what condition may a player leave the playing venue during a game?

options.text: Only in the last round
Only with the permission of the arbiter
At any time freely
Only during the opponent's thinking time

questions.explanation: Per FIDE Laws Article 11.5, players may leave the playing venue during the game only with the permission of the arbiter.

questions.text: What happens if a player makes an illegal move in a standard game and the opponent presses the clock?

options.text: The player immediately loses the game
The position is restored to the moment before the illegal move; the offender's time is penalised
The move is played and is irreversible
The game is restarted from the beginning

questions.explanation: Per FIDE Laws Article 7.5, if during a game it is found that an illegal move was made, the position shall be reinstated to what it was immediately before the illegal move. The clocks shall be adjusted accordingly, including a time penalty.

questions.text: What is the primary goal of FIDE's Anti-Cheating Regulations?

options.text: To punish players who make dubious moves
To protect the integrity of chess competition and deter the use of electronic assistance
To restrict access to strong players at open events
To reduce the number of draws in elite chess

questions.explanation: The FIDE Anti-Cheating Regulations (A09) exist to protect the integrity of chess competition, specifically deterring and detecting the use of external assistance, particularly computer assistance, during games.

questions.text: Which of the following is a valid penalty an arbiter may impose under FIDE Laws Article 12.2?

options.text: Awarding the offending player extra time
Reducing the remaining time of the offending player
Requiring the offending player to replay the entire game
Fining the offending player a monetary amount

questions.explanation: Per Article 12.2, valid arbiter penalties include: warning, increasing the opponent's time, reducing the offender's time, declaring the game lost by the offender, and expulsion. Monetary fines are not a listed chess-game penalty.

questions.text: In a round-robin tournament with an ODD number of players, what happens in each round?

options.text: A player is eliminated
One player receives a bye
Two players must share one board
The tournament pauses for that round

questions.explanation: In a round-robin with an odd number of players, one player receives a bye each round. The Berger table assigns the bye systematically so each player receives it exactly once.

questions.text: What is the defining characteristic of a Knock-out tournament system?

options.text: Players are paired against opponents with equal scores
Every player meets every other player
Players are eliminated after losing a match
Two teams play each member of the other team

questions.explanation: In a knock-out (or elimination) tournament, players are eliminated after losing a match. Winners advance to the next round until only the champion remains.

questions.text: Which Swiss pairing system is the FIDE standard and is required for FIDE-rated events unless another approved system is specified?

options.text: The Monrad System
The McMahon System
The Dutch System
The SSYS System

questions.explanation: Per FIDE Swiss Rules (C04), the Dutch System is the standard FIDE Swiss pairing system. The Baku Acceleration is an FIDE-approved accelerated variant, but the Dutch System is the default standard.

questions.text: In the Baku Acceleration system, what is the purpose of assigning virtual points to the top-ranked players in early rounds?

options.text: To reward players who paid higher entry fees
To ensure top players meet each other earlier in the tournament
To reduce the total number of rounds needed
To compensate for late entries

questions.explanation: The Baku Acceleration assigns virtual rating-based points to the top half of players so that they meet each other earlier in the tournament, reducing early-round mismatches and producing more decisive results at the top from round one.

questions.text: What is the minimum rate of play required for a game to be eligible for FIDE standard rating?

options.text: At least 30 minutes per player for all moves
At least 60 minutes per player for all moves
At least 10 minutes per player for all moves
At least 90 minutes per player for all moves

questions.explanation: Per FIDE Rating Regulations B02.1, for standard rating the rate of play must allow at least 60 minutes for each player to complete all moves. Rapid requires 10–60 minutes; blitz requires 3–10 minutes.

questions.text: What is the K-factor used in the FIDE Elo rating formula for a new player (initial rating period)?
questions.explanation: Per B02.8, the K-factor is 40 for new players (first 30 games or until reaching a published rating). It is 20 for players below 2400 once established, and 10 for players who have ever achieved 2400 or above.

questions.text: What is the minimum FIDE rating required to earn the Grandmaster (GM) title?
questions.explanation: Per FIDE Title Regulations B01.3, a player must achieve a FIDE rating of at least 2500 AND score three GM norms (each with a performance rating of at least 2600) to be awarded the Grandmaster title.

questions.text: How is the FIDE Master (FM) title awarded — what is the requirement?

options.text: Three FM norms and a rating of 2200
Achieving a FIDE rating of 2300 or above
Winning a national championship
Playing 100 rated games

questions.explanation: Per B01.5, the FM title is awarded to any player who achieves a FIDE standard rating of 2300 or above. No norms are required — it is a rating-based title only.

questions.text: What is the recommended minimum table size for an OTB chess game according to FIDE Technical Recommendations?

options.text: 60 cm × 60 cm
70 cm × 70 cm
100 cm × 80 cm

questions.explanation: FIDE Technical Recommendations specify that each player should have sufficient playing space. The recommended minimum table size is approximately 100 cm × 80 cm to comfortably accommodate the board, clock, scoresheets and player materials.

questions.text: What is the recommended king height for a chess set used in a FIDE-rated event?

options.text: 6–8 cm

questions.explanation: FIDE Technical Recommendations specify that the king height should be between 8.5 cm and 10.5 cm for standard FIDE-rated events. The king's base diameter should be 40–50% of its height.

questions.text: In FIDE tournament regulations, what is the standard tiebreak criterion used FIRST when players are equal on points?

options.text: Number of wins
Buchholz score (sum of opponents' scores)
Direct encounter (head-to-head result)
Rating at the start of the event

questions.explanation: Per FIDE General Competition Regulations (C05), in Swiss system events, Buchholz (sum of opponents' final scores) is the most commonly applied first tiebreak. However, specific events may specify direct encounter first — tiebreak order must be announced before the event.

questions.text: A player who withdraws from a tournament before it ends — how are their results treated in terms of FIDE rating?

options.text: All results stand regardless of when the player withdrew
All results are cancelled
Results of opponents who played the withdrawn player may be excluded if the player completed fewer than 50% of their games
The withdrawn player's results are kept; opponents' results against them are cancelled

questions.explanation: Per FIDE regulations, if a player withdraws having completed fewer than 50% of their scheduled games, the results against that player may be excluded from both tiebreak calculations and rating reports depending on the regulation applied.

questions.text: What is the minimum examination pass mark required at a FIDE Arbiter seminar to qualify for the FA (FIDE Arbiter) title application?
questions.explanation: Per FIDE Regulations for Arbiters (B06), candidates must pass the FIDE Arbiter seminar exam with a score of at least 80% to qualify for the FA title application.

questions.text: FIDE awards two arbiter titles: FIDE Arbiter (FA) and International Arbiter (IA). Which title requires the higher level of qualifying events?

options.text: FIDE Arbiter (FA)
International Arbiter (IA)
Both require exactly the same events
Neither — they are awarded simultaneously

questions.explanation: Per B06.1, the IA (International Arbiter) title requires serving as Chief Arbiter or Deputy Chief Arbiter at international qualifying events and accumulating norms at higher-level events than those required for the FA title.

questions.text: Under FIDE Online Chess Regulations (E04), what is a 'hybrid' chess event?

options.text: An event mixing rapid and blitz games
An event combining both over-the-board (OTB) and online play
An event mixing team and individual formats
An event open to both humans and computer programs

questions.explanation: Per FIDE Online Chess Regulations (E04), a hybrid event is one that combines over-the-board play with online play — for example where players are physically present in different locations but compete over an online platform under arbiter supervision.

questions.text: In an online FIDE-rated chess event, who is responsible for ensuring the integrity of the games?

options.text: The platform operator alone
The players themselves
The appointed arbiter, following FIDE Online Chess Regulations
The national federation of the strongest player

questions.explanation: Per FIDE Online Chess Regulations (E04), the appointed arbiter is responsible for the integrity of the event and must apply FIDE regulations adapted for the online environment.

questions.text: A player knocks over several pieces during time trouble. Who is responsible for restoring the position, and when?

options.text: Only the arbiter must restore pieces, only after the game ends
Both the player who knocked pieces over and the opponent must restore them immediately
The player who knocked the pieces over must restore them on their own time; the opponent must stop the clock first
It is left unresolved until the round ends

questions.explanation: Per FIDE Laws Articles 7.3/7.4, if pieces are accidentally displaced, both players are responsible for restoring the position using the scoresheet and the clock if necessary. The arbiter should be called if agreement cannot be reached.

questions.text: In the FIDE Arbiter exam context, what percentage score is generally considered a passing grade, reflecting the standard applied at official FIDE Arbiter seminars?
questions.explanation: FIDE Arbiter seminars require candidates to score at least 80% on the written examination to be eligible to apply for the FIDE Arbiter (FA) title. This portal also uses 75% as a practice pass threshold to prepare candidates.
